thread.title: Dow Jones Industrials: The Beginning Of The End? - Part 3 - SPDR Dow Jones Industrial Average ETF (NYSEARCA:DIA)

author: Income Generator
title: Dow Jones Industrials: The Beginning Of The End? - Part 3 - SPDR Dow Jones Industrial Average ETF (NYSEARCA:DIA)
text:
Stock investors have once again found themselves in an uncertain market environment, and the SPDR Dow Jones Industrial Average ETF ( DIA ) has lost 8.69% since the ETF reached its highs in October. The extent of these declines has caught many investors by surprise and this has led to heightened speculation which suggests the post-2008 bull rally in the industrial sector may have reached its top. Rising interest rates, crashing oil prices, and global trade tensions weigh on growth prospects and generate concerns that the long-term bull market is coming to an end. Many traders have surrendered their long positions in favor of the relative “security” of cash positions. But the recent earnings performances from key holdings in the SPDR Dow Jones Industrials ETF do not match this negative outlook. Ultimately, this suggests rallies may lie ahead for those with long exposure to DIA.
(Source: ETF.com)
The SPDR Dow Jones Industrials ETF has an expense ratio of 0.17% and is largely devoted to the industrial sector (at 22.58% of the total holdings). But the fund is more diversified than most of the other ETFs in the same category. The technology sector accounts for 18.88% of the fund holdings while financials (14.65%), consumer cyclicals (14.63%), and health care stocks (13.35%) make up the remainder of the top five positions. This broad level of diversification contributes a protective layer of sector safety for investors with holding positions in DIA.
(Source: ETFdb.com)
Unfortunately, this level of diversification has failed to give investors safe-haven protection under the current market conditions. Over the last week, we have seen fund outflows of $164.7 million produce a negative influence on DIA valuations. But when we look at the broader flow activity which is present for the fund, these moves start to look much more temporary in nature. Over the last four weeks, DIA shows inflows of $590.3 million. This puts the ETF near the upper end of the category range. When we expand this out further, we can see that the fund has benefited from inflows of $1,594.2 million over the last 13 weeks. As long-term inflows engulf the shorter-term outflows, we can see that market sentiment remains firmly positioned in bullish territory. These trends could continue to favor those with long positions in DIA.
(Source: Author)
Further evidence supporting the bullish stance is apparent in the quarterly earnings results of the fund’s core holdings. Boeing Company ( BA ) makes up 8.69% of the total holdings in DIA, and the stock has fallen 19.11% since it reached prior highs on October 3 rd . Given the strength of the stock’s prior rallies, it is not entirely surprising to see some investors consider surrendering their positions. But this type of activity fails to match the strong underlying fundamentals present within the company. For the third quarter , Boeing showed adjusted earnings of $3.58 per share, which was far above analyst expectations of $3.37 per share. Revenues for the period were also highly impressive at $25.15 billion (against expectations of $23.89 billion).
On an annualized basis, Boeing grew its revenue figure by 3.8%. In addition to this, Boeing raised its earnings forecast to $14.90-15.10 for the full-year period. The prior guidance figures for 2018 indicated an expectation for earnings of $14.30-14.50 per share. If the current projections are realized, Boeing has the potential to hit $100 billion in annual revenues for the first time in the history. Despite all of the recent downside activity, shares of BA stock are still trading higher by 7.60% on a YTD basis.
(Source: Author)
DIA is typically associated with investment exposure to the industrial sector. But it is important to remember that the fund actually devotes 18.88% of its holdings to the technology sector. For a long time, Apple ( AAPL ) has been a leading name in the sector and the company’s performances can have a significant impact on the sentiment directed toward technology stocks as a whole. But recent market declines have been readily apparent in AAPL share prices. The latest market crashes have put AAPL into “bearish correction” territory, and this is significant because the stock makes up a substantial 5.03% of the fund.
Ultimately, Apple represents another example of a company with strong underlying fundamentals, which is currently on the receiving end of a fickle period of panic-selling. Apple generated earnings of $2.91 per share during the fiscal fourth quarter, which surpassed analyst estimates ($2.78 per share) by a wide margin. Apple’s revenue figure for the period ($62.9 billion) was also much higher than prior estimates ($61.57 billion).
Some of the results present in Apple’s most recent report were less encouraging, as the company generated slower iPhone sales (46.89 million) relative to analyst expectations (47.5 million). But these weaknesses were largely offset by the company’s operational efficiency and superior margins. This was evident in the average sale price for the iPhone during the period ($793), and it contributed to Apple’s massive beat on the bottom-line figures for the period. Of course, this strength is not being reflected in share prices, as recent declines have pushed the stock down to levels below $177 per share. Relative to the highs on October 3 rd (at $232.07), AAPL shares have fallen 23.82%.
(Source: Author)
These are troublesome trends, as investors seem to be overlooking evidence of strength in corporate profitability. Fortunately, this is unlikely to continue given the massive technical divergences we are now seeing relative to the stock’s fundamentals. In most cases, I argue that chart analysis is underrated. But this appears to be an example of market irrationality where investors might want to consider reducing its levels of importance in strategic positioning. Fundamental stability in the core holdings of DIA does not reflect the significant weakness which has unfolded over the last several weeks. Long-term inflows directed at the ETF continue to support the bullish outlook for DIA, and these recent price declines have generated new buying opportunities for investors willing to take a contrarian stance in the market.
